finding: At T = 20, moving-resonance suppression survives reference-halo weighting, with a magnitude about 4.7 times smaller than for the selected Gaussian. At the predeclared T = 10 check, the Gaussian and halo-weighted populations give opposite signs despite matching initial density and slope. These are absolute-weighted contributions in one fixed halo-action slice.

prediction_status: All three new populations meet the predeclared magnitude criterion across both sweeps, durations and windows (24/24 comparisons). The accuracy allowance is the larger of 0.0002 and 5% of the forecast magnitude. The moving width-12 Gaussian at T = 10 only narrowly meets the absolute floor. This is a prospective population test within the same prescribed local model, not a qualified 3D halo prediction.
display_scope: Exact sums of recorded kernel-cell contributions, coarsened for display. Bands are pointwise95%t7 intervals of eight independent batches. Gradient bins are not initial-particle cohorts. Lines guide the eye between cells; onlyT10/T20are recorded endpoints. Independent-agreement display uses the declared2e-4 operational scale around the sampling interval, not a rigorous error bound.

heldout_validation.scope: Three prospective populations crossed with two sweeps, two durations and two windows. Correlated comparisons, not24independent physical confirmations. Pointwise95%intervals; accuracy is max(0.0002,5%of the frozen magnitude), with separate operational numerical/window checks. Not a rigorous combined-error bound or a3Dprediction.
